editorial:
Imagine moving into a brand new place with your partner, only for them to leave for a business trip right after. That is exactly what happens to Susan. You get to feel her loneliness as she wanders around the empty flat, waiting for Anders to come home. The whole vibe is very quiet and tense. You start to wonder if she is just imagining things or if there is actually someone sneaking into her home while she sleeps. It feels like a slow build-up of stress that makes you feel just as trapped as she does.

The acting is great because it relies on small expressions rather than big speeches. You will love how the movie blends her scary dreams of being homeless with her actual life. While the pace is a bit slow for some, it really helps you feel her isolation. If you enjoy psychological stories that mess with your head, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: As the story wraps up, you realize that Susan's fears were not just in her head. The movie reveals that her mental state has completely broken down due to her loneliness and anxiety. The twist shows that the lines between her nightmares and reality have blurred. She ends up trapped in a cycle of grief and fear, showing that she cannot escape her own mind even when she is safe inside her own home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow-burn thrillers and character studies.
